description: Mental and emotional symptoms experienced during perimenopause and menopause

entries.title: Mood Swings
entries.description: Rapid, unpredictable changes in emotional state
entries.content: Mood swings during menopause involve sudden shifts from feeling energetic and happy to sad, irritable, or angry. These fluctuations are caused by changing estrogen levels, which affect neurotransmitters like serotonin and dopamine that regulate mood. Mood swings can be distressing and impact relationships and daily functioning.
entries.duration: Common during perimenopause, often improve after menopause
management: Regular exercise to boost mood-regulating neurotransmitters
Maintain social connections and support system
Hormone therapy can help stabilize mood
entries.when_to_see_doctor: If mood swings are severe, disruptive to relationships or work, or accompanied by thoughts of self-harm

entries.title: Anxiety
entries.description: Persistent worry, nervousness, or feelings of unease
entries.content: Anxiety is common during menopause, characterized by excessive worry, restlessness, tension, rapid heartbeat, and difficulty relaxing. Hormonal fluctuations affect brain chemistry and the stress response system. Anxiety can be new or worsen existing anxiety disorders.
management: Relaxation techniques (deep breathing, progressive muscle relaxation)
Anti-anxiety medications or SSRIs/SNRIs if needed
entries.when_to_see_doctor: If anxiety is severe, persistent, interferes with daily life, or includes panic attacks

entries.title: Depression
entries.description: Persistent low mood, sadness, or loss of interest in activities
entries.content: Depression during menopause involves persistent sadness, hopelessness, loss of interest in previously enjoyed activities, changes in appetite, and low energy. Women with a history of major depressive episodes are 59% more likely to experience depression during perimenopause. Hormonal changes affect serotonin and other mood-regulating neurotransmitters.
management: Hormone therapy may help in some cases
entries.when_to_see_doctor: Always seek help for depression, especially if persistent, severe, or includes thoughts of self-harm or suicide

entries.title: Irritability
entries.description: Increased tendency to feel annoyed, frustrated, or angry
entries.content: Irritability during menopause involves a lower threshold for frustration, increased impatience, and quick anger responses. This can strain relationships and is often compounded by other symptoms like poor sleep and hot flashes. Hormonal changes and the stress of managing multiple symptoms contribute to irritability.
management: Communicate with family and friends about what you're experiencing
Vitamin B6 may help with irritability
Hormone therapy or antidepressants if severe
entries.when_to_see_doctor: If irritability is severe or damaging relationships

entries.title: Brain Fog
entries.description: Difficulty with memory, concentration, and mental clarity
entries.content: Brain fog during menopause includes forgetfulness, difficulty concentrating, trouble finding words, and reduced mental sharpness. Women may forget appointments, lose items, or have trouble multitasking. This is caused by hormonal effects on brain function and is often worsened by poor sleep. Brain fog is usually temporary and improves after menopause.
entries.duration: Common during perimenopause, often improves postmenopause
management: Physical exercise to improve brain blood flow
Rule out other causes (thyroid, vitamin deficiencies)
entries.when_to_see_doctor: If cognitive problems are severe, progressive, or include personality changes (could indicate dementia or Alzheimer's)

entries.title: Memory Problems
entries.description: Difficulty remembering names, words, or recent events
entries.content: Memory lapses are common during menopause, including forgetting names, misplacing items, or losing train of thought. This is related to hormonal effects on the hippocampus (memory center) and is often temporary. However, severe memory problems warrant evaluation to rule out other conditions.
entries.when_to_see_doctor: If memory problems are severe, worsening, or include forgetting familiar people, places, or how to do routine tasks

entries.title: Difficulty Concentrating
entries.description: Trouble focusing, maintaining attention, or completing tasks
entries.content: Difficulty concentrating during menopause involves trouble staying focused on tasks, being easily distracted, and struggling to complete work or conversations. This is related to hormonal effects on attention and executive function, and is often worsened by fatigue and sleep problems.
management: Prioritize important tasks when energy is highest
Treat underlying sleep or mood problems
entries.when_to_see_doctor: If severely impacting work or daily functioning

entries.title: Low Self-Esteem
entries.content: Menopause can affect self-esteem due to physical changes, societal attitudes about aging, and hormonal effects on mood. Women may feel less attractive, capable, or valuable, impacting confidence and well-being.
management: Treat physical symptoms that affect self-image
Reframe menopause as a natural life stage
entries.when_to_see_doctor: If low self-esteem is severe or accompanied by depression

entries.title: Panic Disorder
entries.description: Sudden episodes of intense fear with physical symptoms
entries.content: Some women experience panic attacks during menopause - sudden episodes of overwhelming fear accompanied by rapid heartbeat, sweating, trembling, shortness of breath, and feeling of losing control. Hormonal changes can trigger or worsen panic disorder.
entries.when_to_see_doctor: Always seek help for panic attacks, especially if frequent or severe

entries.title: Emotional Sensitivity
entries.content: Increased emotional sensitivity during menopause involves crying more easily, feeling overwhelmed by emotions, or having stronger reactions to situations. This is related to hormonal effects on emotional regulation.
management: Talk to supportive friends or family
entries.when_to_see_doctor: If emotional sensitivity is severely disruptive or accompanied by depression

entries.title: Loss of Motivation
entries.description: Reduced drive, energy, or interest in activities
entries.content: Loss of motivation during menopause involves difficulty starting or completing tasks, reduced interest in hobbies or goals, and feeling unmotivated. This can be related to hormonal changes, fatigue, or depression.
management: Regular exercise to boost energy and mood
entries.when_to_see_doctor: If accompanied by other signs of depression or severely impacting life

entries.title: Social Withdrawal
entries.description: Reduced desire for social interaction or isolation
entries.content: Some women withdraw from social activities during menopause due to embarrassment about symptoms (hot flashes, mood changes), low energy, or depression. Social isolation can worsen mental health symptoms.
management: Maintain social connections even when difficult
Communicate with friends about what you're experiencing
entries.when_to_see_doctor: If social withdrawal is severe or part of depression
